name: INTERACT3
fullName: Care Bundle Approach for Acute Intracerebral Haemorrhage
population: n=7036, ≥18, NIHSS n/a, <6 h from onset
teachingPoint: Establishes care-bundle approach for acute ICH.

name: INTERACT2
fullName: Rapid Blood-Pressure Lowering in Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage
teachingPoint: Supports early BP reduction in ICH; ordinal benefit despite a negative dichotomous primary.

name: ATACH-2
fullName: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage
teachingPoint: More intensive target (<140) gave no benefit and more renal AEs — avoid overshoot below ~140.

name: INTERACT1-4 pooled
fullName: Effects of Blood Pressure Lowering in Relation to Time in Acute Intracerebral Haemorrhage: A Pooled Analysis of the Four INTERACT Trials
population: n=11312, Mean 63 years (SD 12.7); 4066 (35.9%) female, 7246 (64.1%) male, NIHSS Not used; baseline severity handled through the ICH score in the heterogeneity analyses, Median 2.9 h from symptom onset to randomisation (IQR 1.8-4.1); INTERACT1-3 enrolled within 6 h of onset, INTERACT4 within 2 h
finding: Favoured intensive BP lowering: significantly decreased odds of poor physical function (mRS 3-6)
teachingPoint: Supports starting BP lowering as early as possible after ICH — ideally within about 3 hours of onset — while making explicit that the benefit is not mediated by reduced haematoma growth.

name: Deep vs lobar ICH BP meta-analysis
fullName: Functional Outcomes After Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction in Deep and Lobar Intracerebral Hemorrhage
population: n=9022, Mean 63 years; 37% female (both analysis steps), NIHSS Not used; ATACH-2 individual patient data were adjusted for Glasgow Coma Scale score and presence of intraventricular haemorrhage, Acute ICH windows as defined by the three parent trials; the analysis did not stratify by time from onset
finding: DID NOT demonstrate a significant benefit of intensive BP reduction in either location. Step 1: deep OR 0.89, lobar OR 0.92. Step 2 (with INTERACT3 added): deep OR 0.82, lobar OR 0.97. All four confidence intervals cross 1.00.
teachingPoint: Teaches that the deep-versus-lobar question in acute BP management is unresolved: current evidence neither establishes a location-specific benefit nor rules one out, so location should not by itself change the acute BP target.
